This is a substantive geometric construction beyond routine qualifying algebra.

items.title: Global convergence of Morse-potential diffusion on compact Riemannian manifolds of dimension at least two under the Hessian drift threshold
items.author: Laurent Miclo
items.work: On the convergence of global-optimization fraudulent stochastic algorithms
items.difficulty_reason: The result controls almost-sure capture by every global Morse minimum for a degenerate diffusion with an anisotropic Hessian threshold. The proof derives a time-changed non-Markov potential process, establishes localized Bessel comparisons and positive capture probabilities, then combines them through global elliptic returns and a uniform strong-Markov regeneration argument. The fractional-potential extension attains the exact threshold and the positive probability of every minimum in dimension at least2, beyond ordinary doctoral stochastic analysis qualifiers.

items.title: A zero-one freezing law for the infinite-bin model with non-increasing reproduction probabilities
items.author: Bastien Mallein, Sanjay Ramassamy and Arvind Singh
items.work: Freezing in the Infinite-Bin Model
items.difficulty_reason: The proof designs a state-dependent coupling of infinite rank configurations under simultaneous bin-count and cumulative-count inequalities. Its four-case rank selector uses a rejection probability and a conditional replacement variable, and must preserve the exact reproduction-law marginal and the induction order even with infinite configurations. These local constructions then control conditional insertion probabilities and produce the freezing zero-one law for a process with long memory, beyond ordinary doctoral probability qualifiers; ordinary Borel-Cantelli is only the final named prerequisite.

items.title: Regular-variation tail-power criterion for the deterministic freezing type of the infinite-bin model
items.author: Bastien Mallein, Sanjay Ramassamy and Arvind Singh
items.work: Freezing in the Infinite-Bin Model
items.difficulty_reason: The selected criterion requires a uniform hierarchy of reinforced bin growth under regularly varying reproduction laws. The proof extracts the random rank window from the full current configuration, bootstraps its conditional insertion intensity through all bins, and handles the critical slowly varying boundary and first frozen bin. This random-front asymptotic hierarchy exceeds ordinary doctoral probability qualifiers; Freedman conditional laws of large numbers and Karamata estimates are only precisely named prerequisites.

It computes the Hochschild rows of an odd exterior algebra, identifies those rows as diagram Hom complexes, and uses injectivity to collapse the diagram direction and control total parity. The diagram-level derived comparison and uniform spectral-sequence argument exceed ordinary doctoral algebra/topology qualifiers.

items.title: Existence, restriction identity and extremal one-sided Lagrangian minimizers for the forced inviscid periodic Burgers equation, simultaneously for all means

items.source_version: Annales Henri Lebesgue 8 (2025), 873-923; DOI 10.5802/ahl.250; publisher version

The proof extends an interval minimizer backwards through the regeneration times t_k=T_*(t_{k-1}), shows that the intervals tile (-infinity,t], transfers the action additively along the chain, and then obtains extremal elements from finiteness of the interval minimizer sets together with path surgery. The retained core is where the mechanism lives: the explicit 1/(4M) strength comparison of Proposition 2.2 and the T_* finiteness argument of Proposition 2.4, so nothing is assumed that the source does not prove. This is the existence theorem that the introduction states as Theorem 1.4, and it is above ordinary PhD qualification problems in stochastic homogenization or the calculus of variations.

items.difficulty_reason: Supplying the named Brenier existence, smooth regularity, Caffarelli contraction and standard heat-semigroup prerequisites leaves a new source-local regularity mechanism under a Laplacian bound rather than directional Hessian bounds. The proof replaces directional differences by spherical averages, establishes finite integrals and a cofactor integration-by-parts inequality with cutoff boundary terms controlled uniformly, and closes the sharp Lp-to-Linfinity estimate. The required original core then constructs curvature-preserving Ornstein-Uhlenbeck approximations and passes the distributional Laplacian bound to the full-support limit, including complete AppendixA proofs; this is above qualification PDE/optimal transport.

items.title: Robustly faithful representations of a finitely generated non-abelian free group into SL2(R) are Anosov
items.author: León Carvajales; Pablo Lessa; Rafael Potrie
items.work: Quasi-isometric free group representations into SL3(R)
items.source_version: Annales Henri Lebesgue 8 (2025), 965-994; DOI 10.5802/ahl.252; publisher version
items.difficulty_reason: The proof rules out a dense image by a polynomial-trace argument in which the density of finite-order traces 2cos(k pi/n) converts any dense image into an arbitrarily small unfaithful perturbation, so discreteness of the image is forced by robust faithfulness alone. It then passes to PSL2(R), uses the geometrically finite structure of the hyperbolic surface, and eliminates parabolics in two genus cases: for genus zero by perturbing a cusp generator to finite order, and for genus greater than zero by writing the cusp word as a product of commutators and simple loops and applying the retained commutator-submersion lemma to realise the perturbation while deforming only two generators. The conclusion that every element is hyperbolic then yields Anosov, equivalently quasi-isometric, in rank one. This deformation-and-surface-structure combination is research-level and clearly beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations in Lie theory or hyperbolic geometry.

items.title: A criterion for non-robust quasi-isometry in SL3(R): free-group representations with a repeated-eigenvalue word and an aligned loxodromic plane admit arbitrarily small unipotent-word deformations
items.author: León Carvajales; Pablo Lessa; Rafael Potrie
items.work: Quasi-isometric free group representations into SL3(R)
items.source_version: Annales Henri Lebesgue 8 (2025), 965-994; DOI 10.5802/ahl.252; publisher version
items.difficulty_reason: The proof keeps a prescribed word omega fixed while deforming the representation: openness of the power map on loxodromic elements of SL3(R) lets the authors replace the image of one generator so that rho(a)^{-m}rho(a^m)rho(b^n) is an n-th power, which forces rho(omega) to be unchanged along the deformation. A one-parameter deformation of the unstable eigenline of rho(a) is then chosen transverse to the attracting plane, so that the coefficient functional theta_t of that plane changes sign on the two sides of t=0 while the approximating functionals of rho_t(a^p)P_0 converge to theta_t; this pins a parameter t_0 with L_0 contained in rho_{t_0}(a^p)P_0. Both rho_{t_0}(omega^q) and rho_{t_0}(a^p omega^q a^{-p}) then preserve that hyperplane and the latter acts on it as a scalar, so the commutator acts as the identity there and, having determinant one, is unipotent. This is the proposition the paper calls the main step towards its main theorem, and the simultaneous prescription-plus-transversality mechanism in a higher-rank setting is above ordinary PhD qualification problems in Lie theory or geometric group theory.

items.author: Simon Vialaret
items.work: Sharp systolic inequalities for invariant tight contact forms on principal S1-bundles over S2
items.source_version: Annales Henri Lebesgue8(2025),995-1021; DOI10.5802/ahl.253; publisher version
items.difficulty_reason: Supplying the named Reeb-flow, Giroux classification and transverse-action prerequisites leaves a new source-local mechanism that turns an invariant surface of section plus a normal-form potential into a systolic bound. The author derives the Euler-number derivative jump from the solid-torus gluing, proves positivity of the level integral from the differential inequality J-kJprime>0, and closes the sharp inequality for e at least 2 and for e=1 by minimising the auxiliary function g_e. The counted core also constructs glued solid-torus contact forms whose systolic ratio tends to one-half, so sharpness and unattainedness are proved inside the same unit; this is research-level contact dynamics well above qualification topology.

items.title: Every nonnegative discrete distribution with zero in its support is an iid-distance law on a complete separable measured metric space
items.author: Renan Gross
items.work: The distance problem via subadditivity
items.source_version: Annales Henri Lebesgue8(2025),1023-1035; DOI10.5802/ahl.254; publisher version
items.difficulty_reason: Supplying the definition of feasibility and the elementary Bernoulli example leaves a genuinely new inverse construction: the author defines a selection space of eventually constant vectors with the index of last disagreement as distance, and must verify the triangle inequality, completeness, separability and Borel measurability under explicit subadditivity and tail-vanishing hypotheses. The proof then decomposes an arbitrary discrete law into dyadic subdistributions, telescopes the conditional probabilities beta_n so that the total mass of the non-default choices is finite, and matches both the atom at zero and every positive atom exactly. No limit of finite approximations is taken, which is precisely what keeps the space separable; this construction is above ordinary qualification probability and metric geometry.

items.title: Equiaffine immersions of closed oriented volume-preserving three-manifolds produce flat SL4/SL3 extensions and vanishing Chern–Simons invariants
items.author: Andreas Čap; Keegan J. Flood; Thomas Mettler
items.work: Flat extensions of principal connections and the Chern--Simons 3-form
items.source_version: Annales Henri Lebesgue8(2025),1037-1059; DOI10.5802/ahl.255; publisher version
items.difficulty_reason: The counted proof lies above ordinary qualification differential geometry because SL(4,R)/SL(3,R) is not a symmetric space and the bracket of two transversal components has a non-zero scalar component, so the general flat-extension theorem does not apply automatically. The authors lift a volume-preserving frame to an SL(4,R) frame using the chosen transversal, recover theta=F^*(mu^top) from the volume compatibility of the immersion, and deduce flatness of the transversal connection from the volume-form lemma. They then read the transversal component of the pulled-back Maurer-Cartan equation to see that the scalar part of the bracket vanishes, which supplies the hypothesis of the counted flat-extension theorem and yields vanishing of the Chern-Simons invariant.

items.title: Twisted Patterson--Sullivan partial-shadow bounds for symmetric finitely supported admissible walks on non-elementary relatively hyperbolic groups
items.author: Matthieu Dussaule; Longmin Wang; Wenyuan Yang
items.work: The growth of the Green function for random walks and Poincaré series
items.source_version: Annales Henri Lebesgue8(2025),1061-1107; DOI10.5802/ahl.256; publisher version
items.difficulty_reason: Supplying the named Patterson--Sullivan existence, Busemann-cocycle continuity, relative Ancona and quasi-conformality prerequisites leaves a source-local partial-shadow estimate in the twisted transition-point setting: the lower bound is reduced to positive measure of a loxodromic inverse shadow combined with equivariance and the coarse Busemann cocycle, while the upper bound combines relative Ancona multiplicativity along transition points with the conical Radon--Nikodym derivative and constants uniform in r and in the group element. The mechanism is not the classical Sullivan shadow lemma: the shadows are cut out by (eta,L)-transition points, the constants must be uniform in the group element, and the authors record that the upper bound for the usual shadow remains unknown. Adapting the argument of [Yan22, Lemmas 4.1 and 4.2] to these Green-function-twisted PS measures, with Lemma 4.6 replacing Lemma 2.19 there, is above ordinary qualification hyperbolic geometry and probability.

items.title: Closures of higher-rank Voronoi cells for admissible discrete sets decompose into almost-orthogonal scalar Voronoi polyhedra
items.author: Omid Amini; Noema Nicolussi
items.work: Higher rank inner products, Voronoi tilings and metric degenerations of tori
items.source_version: Annales Henri Lebesgue8(2025),1109-1188; DOI10.5802/ahl.257; publisher version
items.difficulty_reason: After the elementary convexity of a higher rank Voronoi cell and the induced filtration are supplied, the authors must still recover the whole closure of the cell from the scalar Voronoi cells of the successive graded projections. The inclusion is extracted coordinate by coordinate from the lexicographic inequalities using the Lifting Lemma, and the reverse inclusion is proved through strict inequalities on products of interiors of the scalar cells, together with the translated-set reduction for a general site. The mechanism is the interaction of a lexicographic order with an almost orthogonal decomposition that need not be orthogonal, and it is precisely the structural statement explaining why higher rank Voronoi cells fail to be closed; this is research-level asymptotic convex and polyhedral geometry, not a qualification exercise.

items.author: Omid Amini; Noema Nicolussi

items.difficulty_reason: The counted lower bound is not a routine application of the upper-bound constructions: the proof assigns to every prime power exactly dividing n a weight on each cycle of a generator, then shows that the total weight of each prime power is at least b(p^r), by a case analysis over the exceptional orders 2,3,4,5,7 and the exception families 6, 12 and 10-14, with the correction terms 11 and 20 when 3 and 2, respectively 3 and 4, exactly divide n. Reaching that point needs the source-local structural theory of cycles of a cyclic poset automorphism, including the extension remark and the four lemmas on how many cycles of length divisible by p^r, 4 or 2p a generator must contain, each proved by constructing an extra automorphism from a symmetry or complement of the height-one posets involved. The upper bound is equally constructive, combining the b(n)n-point posets with an ordinal sum and the exceptional 20-point poset for Z_12, so the exact minus-one correction is essential; this is well above ordinary PhD qualifying material.

items.title: Holomorphic compactly supported regularizing perturbations of Green-hyperbolic operators with discrete exceptional parameters
items.author: Christopher J. Fewster
items.work: Modified Green-Hyperbolic Operators
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 19 (2023) article 057, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2023.057; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The proof synchronizes analytic Fredholm inverses across every Sobolev order and upgrades them to the bounded-convergence topology of smooth compactly supported functions. It extends the compact-support inverse to the LF test-function space, constructs both Green operators and proves the precise causal support alternative. A separate holomorphic support argument recovers ordinary Green propagation for support-nonincreasing modifications, so this is more than applying the analytic Fredholm theorem at one Hilbert-space level.

source_check.note: The complete Theorem3.1, Theorem5.1, Corollary5.2, Lemma5.3 and the technical bounded-convergence support lemmas A.2–A.6 are supplied. The standing manifold is a globally hyperbolic spacetime with finitely many connected components and fixed topologically regular compact K; P acts on smooth scalar functions. A(0)=0, range A(lambda) is supported in K, the stated distribution/Sobolev extensions improve total regularity by delta=beta+gamma>0, and A(lambda)E+/- is holomorphic at all relevant Sobolev levels. The full source assumptions (a)–(d) and the stronger (d-prime) alternative are retained literally, without reducing them to the misleading shorthand smoothing perturbation. Established Green-hyperbolic extension theory and analytic Fredholm theory are background; the new smooth/LF inversion, Green identities, parameter continuity and support construction are fully proved here. The dual-kernel comparison3.5 and special integral-kernel corollaries are not counted separately. items.title: Strictly convex Pfaff-Darboux representations adapted to a positive Legendrian foliation for a torsion-free affine connection
items.author: Robert L. Bryant
items.work: On the Convex Pfaff-Darboux Theorem of Ekeland and Nirenberg
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 19 (2023) article 060, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2023.060; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The proof upgrades positivity only along the prescribed Legendrian leaves to strict positivity of every coordinate Hessian on the ambient tangent space. It successively changes the Pfaff coordinates by quadratic corrections, a one-variable convex reparametrization and controlled positive linear mixtures. The final perturbation makes all coefficient functions positive while preserving the given foliation and the exact one-form representation, an additional construction beyond the ordinary Pfaff-Darboux normal form.

source_check.note: The complete Theorem3.3 constructive proof is included. M is a smooth manifold with a torsion-free affine connection, omega has fixed Pfaff rank k-1 through omega wedge (domega)^k=0 and omega wedge (domega)^(k-1) nowhere zero, and the given omega-Legendrian foliation has leafwise positive-definite symmetric covariant derivative S^nabla omega. The result is local at every point, with strictly nabla-convex functions constant on the prescribed leaves and positive smooth coefficients. The classical Pfaff-Darboux theorem is explicitly prior background; the author actually gives all of the new convexity and positivity adjustments. The unadapted corollary and Euclidean special case are not additional counted units. items.difficulty_reason: The theorem treats arbitrary small groupoids and their rings with enough idempotents, where a global unit and finite-dimensional group algebra cannot be assumed. items.difficulty_reason: Infinite Hankel inversion requires absolute control of double sums; finite inverse identities do not justify associating the infinite matrix products. The author proves separate moment and reproducing-kernel coefficient bounds by q-Pochhammer inductions and shows stability under finite initial recurrence changes. Their combination yields superexponential decay of the shifted coefficient-moment products and the strong summability needed for a valid inverse.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Full Theorem1.9 for a symmetric Hamburger probability-moment problem with infinite support and all moments, Jacobi diagonal a_n=0, positive recurrence b_n, and b_(n-1)/b_n<=q for some0<q<1 and all sufficiently large n. Retain definitions U_n=s_(2n)/(b_0^2...b_(n-1)^2), V_n=b_0...b_(n-1)*c_n and c_n=sqrt(A_(n,n)), where A is the reproducing-kernel coefficient matrix. U_n,V_n,c_n*sqrt(s_(2n)) are bounded and sum_l c_l*abs(s_(l+m)) is finite for every m>=0. The supplied Lemma2.1 yields AH=HA=I with entrywise absolute convergence. No bounded-operator inverse interpretation on l2, uniqueness among all infinite inverses or polynomial-growth relaxation is added.

items.difficulty_reason: The adjoint representation up to homotopy of an inverse-image Lie algebroid is not just the pullback adjoint bundle. items.difficulty_reason: Beyond the ordinary Sobolev and Birkhoff normal-form prerequisites, the authored proof establishes cluster-sensitive weighted Poisson-bracket estimates for an infinite family of super-actions. items.difficulty_reason: After the named David-integrability and removability prerequisites are supplied, the original local core constructs continuous factors of discontinuous Bowen-Series maps by cyclic quotient and proves the degree, analytic pieces, critical data and normalized circle conjugacy. items.difficulty_reason: After the classical cuboid/fibre criterion and the two-prime positive fibre decomposition of Lam--Leung Theorem 3.3, the proof still has to propagate all remaining cyclotomic divisors across successively finer congruence grids. The author uses CRT-normalized fibres to keep every one of the p smaller-grid weights indivisible by q, enabling the exponent-amplifying induction. items.difficulty_reason: The written proof of Theorem 1.1 occupies only lines 1120--1140, and that is exactly the point: it is the top of a source-local chain whose own content is the difficulty. The authors must split the Nehari-type constraint into k localized pieces N_j^- around the k singular poles, prove for each piece that the levels separate as c_{lambda,j} < (2/N) A_mu^{N/4} - chi lambda^2 < hat c_{lambda,j} so that the critical concentration level 2 A_0^{N/4}/N is excluded, and only then may Ekeland's principle be applied to produce a bounded Palais-Smale sequence and, via Lemma 4.2, a strong limit. The distinctness of the k solutions (Remark 3.2) is itself a source-local argument. Concentration-compactness at the critical Sobolev exponent and Ekeland's principle are named prerequisites, but their interaction with the two-sided bounds (1.3) on the multipolar Rellich-type potential V is new and is not reachable by a standard qualifying-exam treatment of fourth-order critical problems.

Multiplicity then comes from genus theory. Concentration-compactness, the Pohozaev identity and the genus are named prerequisites, but the truncation threshold, the multiplier estimate and the exclusion of the critical level are new and specific to this Kirchhoff-Schrodinger-Poisson system; this is research-level analysis well beyond any qualifying examination.

The proof must analyse the monotonicity of gamma_B on each I_n and locate the unique critical point alpha_n where gamma_B' vanishes, then choose interval by interval between xi-bar_{B^c}^+ and its negative so that the resulting piecewise xi-bar_B is injective, and finally verify injectivity across five distinct configurations of points, carrying the argument separately through the case of finitely many graininesses and the case of countably infinitely many. items.difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the headline consistency result of the article: the deep-learning estimator of the callable-bond price in a discretised fractional Black-Scholes market converges in L1 to the true price. Its complete proof has to pass from the almost-sure convergence of the discretised expectation by the strong law of large numbers and dominated convergence, rewrite the estimator as an empirical average over the same path grid, isolate the event on which the estimated call time differs from the true one, and then transfer that stopping-time error into a price error by Cauchy-Schwarz against the square-integrability of the discounted payoff, invoking the source-local convergence of the estimated optimal call time. It is graded H2 rather than H3 because each ingredient is a quantitative convergence estimate rather than a new structural mechanism: the counted body itself performs the final assembly of prerequisites that the delivered item retains uncounted as complete context.

Its complete proof must first record the evenness of the functional and the Palais-Smale property supplied by the source-local compactness lemma, and must then verify the two geometric hypotheses of the symmetric mountain pass theorem in two separate frequency regimes: below half of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue it has to produce a strict local minimum at the origin through a Poincare estimate with an epsilon absorption and the growth conditions on the perturbation, while above that threshold it has to split the space along the eigenvalues of the Dirichlet Laplacian, choose the index at which the frequency crosses the spectrum and prove positivity of the functional on small spheres of the complementary subspace, using the sign of the frequency against that spectral splitting. This is a genuine research-level minimax verification for a fourth-order coupled system; it is graded H2 rather than H3 because the argument applies a named abstract critical point theorem with standard eigenvalue splitting rather than introducing a new compactness or deformation mechanism, the necessary compactness being supplied by the Palais-Smale lemma retained as complete context.

Its complete proof must set up the weighted-degree expansion of the squared-norm Hamiltonian, transfer the hypothesis on the two scalar polynomials into a statement about the vanishing set of the highest weighted part, locate the support of the Bendixson-compactified Hamiltonian vector field with respect to the two coordinate axes and the diagonal, split the argument into the two cases in which the first weight is smaller or larger than the second, and in each case identify the Newton diagram vertices and edges, their types and the associated Hamiltonians, and then verify that no associated Hamiltonian carries a factor of the printed special form. items.title: Global existence and the uniform a priori estimate in homogeneous Besov spaces for the 2D inviscid magnetic Benard system (Theorem 1.1)

items.difficulty_reason: After the paper's Section 2 toolkit (Littlewood--Paley decomposition, Bernstein inequalities, Besov embedding, interpolation and derivative properties, product and commutator estimates) is supplied as context, the counted proof still has to build a source-local mechanism. It must first extract a horizontal dissipation term for the velocity from the temperature equation and a vertical dissipation term from the magnetic equation, through the cancellation identities (3.4), (3.6), (3.7) and (3.8) (source lines 544--609); then combine those four frequency-localized identities with two large constants C1 and C2 into the augmented energy functionals and prove their coercivity against the negative cross terms by Bernstein inequality in the two frequency regimes j at most 0 and j at least -1 (lines 611--666 and 729--777); then sum over the dyadic blocks in the two Besov norms and bound every nonlinear and commutator term by the product of the two energy functionals (lines 677--693 and 850--884); and finally close the Lyapunov-type differential inequality (3.26) under the smallness condition on the supremum of the energy, which is what forces the life span to be infinite by the bootstrap argument (lines 887--908). The named analytic ingredients are classical, but their assembly here is paper-specific and coercivity-free: the dissipation is recovered only from the coupling structure, the two frequency regimes require an induction that is made self-consistent through the constants C1 and C2, and the resulting estimate is uniform in the life span. That is clearly beyond an ordinary PhD qualifying examination on the Euler, Navier--Stokes or MHD equations, and it is graded H2 rather than H3 because each individual ingredient is a named classical estimate rather than a new research device.

items.title: Homogenization in the critical case for an optimal control problem with dynamic boundary conditions on microscopic particles: the homogenized system and the limit adjoint problem (Theorem 5.1)
items.author: Jesus Ildefonso Diaz; Tatyana A. Shaposhnikova; Alexander V. Podolskiy

items.difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the paper's main homogenization result and its proof is the whole difficulty of the unit. After the setting, the adjoint problem, the a priori estimates and the non-local in time operators of Sections 2 to 4 are supplied as context, the proof must still build a multi-scale construction: it constructs the auxiliary functions solving the model boundary-value problems on the dilated cells (lines 1286--1293) and glues them into the global alternating test functions associated with the controlled and the uncontrolled particles (lines 1298--1313); it applies the surface-to-volume averaging convergence principle (lines 1361--1374) so that the boundary integrals over the particle boundaries of the critical case become volume terms carrying the two thresholds of the limit problem and the strange terms; it then runs four separate passages to the limit for the state equation (Steps A.1 to A.4, lines 1318--1601), where the surfaces of the two particle families must be tracked separately and the limits of the surface terms are identified through the three auxiliary non-local operators; it then repeats the analysis for the adjoint equation (Steps B.1 to B.3, lines 1616--1798), where the combination multiplying the limit adjoint state only collapses to the closed form of the limit operator after the second relation of Lemma 4.1 is used (lines 1657--1671); and it closes by upgrading the subsequence convergences to the whole sequences through the well-posedness of the limit problem (lines 1817--1819). The critical scaling of the radius is exactly what makes the strange terms appear simultaneously in the state equation, in the adjoint equation and in the cost functional, and there is no textbook or qualifying-exam counterpart: each step is a source-local device of this paper. The unit is therefore graded H3 rather than H2.

items.title: Existence of a positive solution for a generalized quasilinear Schrodinger equation with asymptotically linear nonlinearity via the Nehari manifold (Theorem 1.1)

items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the paper's main existence theorem, and its written proof (source lines 1086--1114) is short precisely because it is the top of a source-local chain: the difficulty is the chain, which is delivered in full. Because the nonlinearity is only asymptotically linear, the mountain-pass geometry alone cannot produce a nontrivial solution and the fixed-sign Nehari manifold is not a manifold, so the authors work on the Nehari manifold split into two pieces through the auxiliary function and the map n, and the proof must (i) treat the easy cases through Propositions 3.14 and 3.15, where Ekeland variational principle is legitimised on the constrained set by the lemma preventing the limiting point from reaching the boundary (line 842), and where the concentration-compactness lemma for Palais-Smale sequences together with the norm equivalence turns the weak limit into a strong one (lines 847--850 and 884--895); (ii) in the remaining case, where the barycentric infimum is strictly larger than the limiting level, construct the modified path built from the dilation parameter and the scaling that returns the translated ground state to the Nehari manifold, whose properties are exactly Lemmas 3.16 to 3.20, including the reformulation of hypothesis (A11) as an interval condition and the strict inequality for the path level (lines 1007--1084); and (iii) run a deformation argument on the Nehari manifold to build a continuous map of a ball into its own boundary that is the identity on the boundary, a contradiction of the quoted topological fact (lines 1090--1110), after which sign-definiteness, elliptic regularity and the maximum principle upgrade the critical point to a positive solution (lines 1111--1113). Minimax theory on a Nehari manifold for a non-local quasilinear operator, with concentration compactness and a barycentre argument, is research-level material with no qualifying-exam counterpart, so the unit is graded H3.

items.title: Global asymptotic stability of the infection equilibrium of a delayed HIV model with CTL immune response and immune impairment (Theorem 3.4)

items.difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the paper's strongest dynamical conclusion: the global asymptotic stability of the infection equilibrium of a four-dimensional delayed HIV model that carries a logistic proliferation of target cells, a saturating incidence, an immune-impairment term in the CTL equation and three independent delays. After the well-posedness, the next infection operator, the equilibria and the characteristic-equation results are supplied as context, the proof still has to build a source-local object: the two-part Lyapunov functional N = N_1 + N_2, whose first part is a sum of the fundamental function at the four equilibrium coordinates and whose second part consists of two delay integrals with the correctly weighted integrands (lines 681--695); it then has to differentiate that functional along the flow, insert the four equilibrium identities to replace the production, infection and clearance parameters (lines 733--742), and reduce the resulting expression, by repeated regrouping and by the logarithmic bookkeeping of the fundamental function, to a sum of negative definite squares and of terms of the shape u - 1 - ln u, which is where the strict positivity of the logistic coefficient under the condition $x_{\rm max}(r-d) < r x^{*}$ is used (lines 744--827); and it must then identify the largest invariant subset of the zero set of the derivative and invoke LaSalle invariance to conclude (lines 828--834). The method is classical but its execution is entirely paper-specific: the weights of the delay integrals and the cancellation pattern have to be found, and the reduction is a long non-obvious algebraic chain that no qualifying examination would ask for, so the unit is graded H2 rather than H3 because every ingredient is a named classical device rather than a new research mechanism.

items.title: Soundness of the relativised safe-recursion function algebras: the permutation-of-prefixes algebra captures polynomial time and the nested algebra captures elementary computation

Soundness is proved by induction on the definition of f: the initial functions are polynomial time and the schemes are handled one by one, with each oracle call replaced by an explicitly bounded function computing its graph via the Bounding Lemma; the recursion case is then evaluated by a course-of-values recursion along the permutation-of-prefixes order whose lookup table must be shown to have polynomial size, using the m! permutations of the prefixes of a list and a bound on the growth rate, with the nested/elementary case requiring a separate argument because the safe inputs of recursive calls must be bounded before the table can be stored. items.title: The divergence-graph edge algorithm for equal-length horocyclic suffixes: linear-time certification of close successors and computation of the uncancelable clique by a finite-state machine

items.difficulty_reason: The counted proof is the paper's own correctness argument for the finite-state machine that decides divergence-graph edges between horocyclic suffixes of equal length, and it is not a qualification exercise. Even with the standing assumptions, the horocyclic normal form of Section 5.1 and the cancellation lemmas of Section 5.2 supplied, the author has to build the state - the subwords u_1, u_2 and u_3, u_4 (or u_5, u_6) of the two horocyclic suffixes, the clique K of uncancelable letters, the bit b recording which word owns the cancelable letters, and the two subword indices n_w and n_v - and then verify five interlocking update rules: the index update, the bit flip forced when one word has moved on to a later subword, the adding letter, the processing of the canceling letter together with the deletion of the letters that it forbids, and the closing bit-flip check. The mathematical content is the invariant maintained across those rules, that K is always a clique commuting with every surviving subword, and the two-sided conclusion: any failure of a check is exactly a pair of uncancelable letters, while a successful run computes K(v,w), the word of cancelable letters, and the side of the pair on which that word must be written. items.title: Non-vanishing of the layered minors of the Fourier matrix of order $pq$

items.difficulty_reason: Even with the paper's own algebraic-number-theory preliminaries supplied - the splitting of the rational prime p in Z[zeta_n] and the identification of the residue field Z[zeta_n]/(1-zeta_p) as the field with p^{phi(m)} elements together with the primitivity of the image of zeta_r there (Lemma 3 and Lemma 4 of the delivered unit), the Dedekind-domain divisibility remark (Remark 2) and Frenkel's multiplicity bound (Lemma 5) - the counted main theorem is not a qualification exercise. The counted proof has to turn the vanishing relation into a single polynomial r(x) with the minimal power of 1-zeta_p divided out, homogenise it into the two-variable polynomial g(x,y), split the index set J into the r layers J_r^k, assemble the |L| x |L| layered system T_t = sum_{k in L} omega_r^{ptk} S_k, reduce the entire system modulo the prime ideal (1-zeta_p) so that Zhang's finite-field Chebotarev theorem becomes applicable to the layered matrix R-bar, and then run a genuine induction on the number of non-empty layers: invert R-bar, use Frenkel's lemma to force the coefficients of the smallest layer S_{k_1} to be divisible by 1-zeta_p, delete that layer from the reduced system, observe that the surviving matrix D-bar is again a square submatrix of the finite-field Fourier matrix and therefore still invertible, and repeat until every coefficient z_j is divisible by 1-zeta_p, contradicting the choice of r(x). Recognising that the reduced system keeps the same Chebotarev type at every step, and that Zhang's hypotheses (primitivity of p in Z_r and p > Gamma_r) survive the peeling, is a research-level assembly well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations in number theory.

items.title: Regularity and well-posedness of the KL-regularized stochastic control problem for fine-tuning diffusion models

Differentiability of the control is obtained from the smoothing effect of the Gaussian noise through the integration-by-parts formula for the Gaussian density, applied to the derivative of the conditional expectation of the gradient of the value function, and the Lipschitz property of that derivative is then extracted from the same identity; only after the control has been shown to be Lipschitz, differentiable and gradient Lipschitz can the regularity of the value function itself be propagated one step backwards. After the proof of Lemma 1 the paper opens a run-in block headed Proof of Theorem 1 and proves the theorem there in one paragraph plus one displayed equation plus one closing paragraph, and that block is the only proof of the counted theorem anywhere in the paper. The proof's structure is as follows. It fixes the alternating binary string of length l and recalls that its whole index sequence is a diffsequence with l-1 hops, so that psi of that string at l-1 hops equals l. It then instantiates Lemma 1, whose statement is psi_{s^(1)}(h) <= psi_s(h+1) + 3h + 2, along the chain of successive expansions with h = l-1-i, obtaining one inequality for each i from 1 to l-1. Summing those l-1 inequalities telescopes the psi terms and leaves a constant term that is the sum of the arithmetic progression 3(l-i-1)+2; the display evaluates it to l + 3(l-1)(l-2)/2 + 2(l-1) = (3l^2-3l+2)/2. Since a colouring of length l times 4^(l-1) then admits no monochromatic diffsequence of length k for every k greater than (3l^2-3l+2)/2, the paper concludes Delta(D,k) >= l times 4^(l-1), and finally chooses the largest admissible l by inverting the quadratic, l = floor( sqrt( 2(k-1)/3 + 1/4 ) + 1/2 ), which turns the bound into the closed form displayed in the counted statement. items.title: Random domain decomposition for parabolic PDEs on graphs: the convergence theorem (Theorem 2.3)
items.author: Mart\'in Hern\'andez

items.difficulty_reason:
Counted unit: the paper's convergence theorem for the continuous random batch method, printed as Theorem 2.3 of the paper (source0.tex lines 331--337; the environment carries the optional title Convergence and the source label th:convergence), delivered together with the paper's own complete proof of it at source0.tex lines 675--1128. The statement is that for the parabolic problem on the graph, its random-batch approximation and the randomized coefficients, the quantity Lambda measuring the variance of the randomization is uniformly bounded in the batch step size and the mean-square error between the two solutions is bounded, uniformly in time, by a constant times the square root of the L1 norm of Lambda times the step size h, with a constant independent of h. It is the paper's main result: the abstract advertises exactly this first-order mean-square convergence of the random batch method at the level of the partial differential equation, without any preliminary discretization in space or time.

The author's proof is complete and extends over roughly four hundred and fifty lines of the source. The author forms the difference of the two solutions, differentiates its squared L2 norm on each randomization interval, decomposes the resulting bilinear expression into the four groups of terms produced by the randomized coefficients, the randomized source and the randomized interval selection, and estimates each group separately: the leading terms are absorbed into the unperturbed energy identity, the remaining ones are bounded by Cauchy-Schwarz, by the boundedness of the coefficients and by the definition of Lambda, and the sums over the random batches are replaced by their expectations using the exchangeability of the batches. The resulting differential inequality is closed by Gronwall's lemma, which produces a bound with an exponential factor in the final time, and the last step converts the surviving double integral of the time derivative of the random solution into a single factor of the step size by first proving an absolute-continuity estimate for the random solution, and then invokes the energy estimate of the paper's well-posedness theorem for the random system to bound the remaining norm by a constant that is independent of h. The proof therefore depends on the paper's own maximal-regularity theorem, on the well-posedness theorem for the random system, on the boundedness lemma for Lambda, and on the whole machinery of the randomized decomposition, all of which are retained in the delivered document.

Carrying this out requires, beyond the standard energy method for parabolic problems, the randomization of a domain decomposition with a non-overlapping cover of the graph, the correct splitting of the consistency error into the terms that can be absorbed and the terms that must be paid for by Lambda, the interchange of the expectation with the time integral over a random number of intervals, and the careful tracking of the constants so that none of them depends on the step size. No qualifying examination poses this: the argument is the technical core of a research paper on random domain decomposition for partial differential equations on graphs, it is stated for a general graph with piecewise smooth coefficients and boundary data, and the constant is required to be uniform in the batch step size. That places the unit in the research range: H3.

items.title: On adjoint orbits in nilpotent ideals of a Borel subalgebra: the intersection theorem (Theorem 3.2)

items.difficulty_reason:
Counted unit: the paper's intersection theorem for closed Borel-stable subsets, printed as Theorem 3.2 of the paper (source0.tex lines 330--333), delivered together with the paper's own complete proof of it at source0.tex lines 334--404. The statement is that the intersection of two non empty closed B-stable subsets of m^bullet is non empty, for an arbitrary nilpotent ideal m of the Borel subalgebra b of a complex finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra; it is the theorem that supplies the uniqueness half of the paper's main result (the abstract's unique closed B-orbit in m^bullet), and the paper's own stated main result (printed as Theorem 1.1, source0.tex lines 106--111) carries no proof anywhere in the paper, so the counted unit is the paper's main proved theorem rather than a formal restatement of an unproved one.

The author's proof is complete and is carried out at the level of coordinate rings. After localising the coordinate ring of m at the product phi of the coordinate functions attached to the minimal roots of m, and identifying m^bullet with the non-vanishing locus of phi, the author splits the coordinate ring of m^bullet as the coordinate ring of m_0^bullet plus the kernel of the comorphism of the projection, using the B_0-equivariant projection of m^bullet onto m_0^bullet. Taking a proper B-stable ideal J, the author observes that its image is a B_0-stable ideal in the coordinate ring of m_0^bullet, where the open B_0-orbit of m_0 (Richardson) forces that image to be either zero or the whole ring. In the second case the author uses that the group M_0 with Lie algebra m_0 is unipotent to average an element f of J with f + g equal to the constant 1 along M_0, obtaining non constant elements f-tilde in the m_0-invariants of J and g-tilde in the m_0-invariants of the kernel whose sum is a constant; the weight decomposition in the negative semi-group generated by the minimal roots, together with the proposition proved immediately before the counted theorem (that those invariants reduce to the polynomial ring on the minimal-root coordinates), lets the author multiply g-tilde by a power of phi and land inside that polynomial ring, which is impossible for a non zero element of the kernel. Hence the image of every proper B-stable ideal is zero. The conclusion is the ideal-theoretic form of the statement: two proper B-stable ideals can never sum to the unit ideal, so two non empty closed B-stable subsets of m^bullet must meet.

Carrying this out requires the invariant theory of unipotent group actions, the dense-orbit theorem of Richardson and the theorem of Rosenlicht that the B-invariant rational functions on m_0 are constant, the weight bookkeeping for semi-invariant regular functions with weights in the negative semi-group generated by the minimal roots, the localisation dictionary between the open subset m^bullet and its coordinate ring, and the translation between closed B-stable subsets and B-stable ideals. No qualifying examination poses this: the argument is the technical heart of a research paper on B-orbits in nilpotent ideals, it is stated for an arbitrary nilpotent ideal in an arbitrary type, and the paper's introduction says that no such general statement was available in the literature. That places the unit in the upper qualifying-to-research range: H2.

The statement is that using the control u = u-bar + u_d renders the system x-dot = a(x) + b(x)u + d(t,x) asymptotically stable, where u-bar is a control law assumed to stabilize the undisturbed system with a strictly positive definite Lyapunov function V whose derivative is negative along the undisturbed controlled trajectories, where b(x) has rank n for all x, and where the disturbance is bounded in norm by a known function lambda with |d| strictly below lambda; the robustifying term is u_d = -(lambda/|grad V|) b-dagger grad V with b-dagger the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse.

The author's proof is complete and short: it follows the Lyapunov redesign method of Khalil Chapter 14.2, differentiates V along the trajectories of the disturbed closed loop, splits the derivative into the undisturbed part (which is negative by hypothesis) plus the terms produced by the robustifying control and by the disturbance, bounds the two new terms by |d| times |grad V| and by -lambda times |grad V| using Cauchy-Schwarz, and concludes that the derivative is bounded above by (|d| - lambda) times |grad V|, which is strictly negative because |d| is strictly below lambda. The proof then closes by recording, from the rank hypothesis on b(x) and the properties of the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse, that b b-dagger grad V equals grad V, so that the robustifying term indeed contributes the exact negative multiple of |grad V| that the estimate uses.

The proposition asserts that the class of truncated cubic graphs is spectrally determined, and the proof is a genuine spectral-reconstruction argument: from the spectrum of T(G) one first recovers the order 3n and the presence of n triangles, then uses the spectral invariance of the number of closed 4-walks together with the fact that T(G) has no 4-cycles and hence only trivial closed 4-walks, to force H to have no 4-cycles either; that in turn forces the triangles of H to be pairwise disjoint and any two triangles to share at most one edge, after which the graph G' on the triangles, with adjacency inherited from H, satisfies H=T(G').
